zones.label: Notice
zones.summary: Kindness often starts by noticing how someone else may be feeling.
facts: Look for a person sitting alone or having trouble joining.
Noticing is the first step toward helping someone belong.

zones.label: Invite
zones.summary: A simple invitation can open a place in the group.
facts: Use friendly words such as “Would you like to play?”
Give the other person time to answer.
An invitation is kind even when the person chooses something else.

zones.label: Play Together
zones.summary: Including others means everyone has a real way to contribute.
facts: Listen to different ways of playing.
Make space for different bodies, skills, and interests.

zones.label: Help Repair
zones.summary: Mistakes can become kind moments when people help fix what happened.
facts: Say sorry when your action caused harm.
Help rebuild, clean up, or try again.
Repair is about caring for the person and the problem.

quiz.question: Which step begins when you see someone sitting alone?
Which step uses friendly words to open the game to someone?
Which step gives every person a meaningful role?
Which step includes apologizing and helping rebuild?
